item.description: (...) se sin cuid de dh’fhaclan a chula [sic] mi bho chionn beagan bhlidhnachan [sic] air ais ’nuair a bha m’Athair is na coimhearsnaich mun chuairt an so a’ bruidhinn a’ Ghaidhlig ged is ainneamh a tha i air a’ bruidhinn aig an làtha an diugh.
this word was usually applied to any young animal or child which showed great energy and very active when playing.
this was the smallest pig or pup in the litter and it usually implied being a weakling.
a volume of water coming from a pipe usually where the water was got for the house.
a very dry bit of peat broken off the main peat.
the bit of ground or the lair where the peats were spread out to dry.

although this word meaning (hide) in in [sic] Gaelic was used about here when a person was getting any little odds and ends for nothing and very often applied if the ghillie got anything home out of the larder during the stalking season.
this was applied to a person who was in the huff and was not speaking.
the chase or pursuit or the nearest other Gaelic word I can think of being ‘ruaig’.
a person of low or humble position.
This is my own idea of spelling these words as I have never seen them written.
